name: layover-pilot
description: Practical, conservative layover planning with source-backed airport guidance and explicit uncertainty.

interface.longDescription: Make the most of the time between flights. Layover Pilot works out a conservative usable window for your connection, helps you decide whether to stay airside or whether leaving the airport may fit, and surfaces source-backed airport facilities, layover options and stopover programmes. It accounts for known baggage, terminal, transfer and return-to-gate constraints, keeps unknowns explicit, and links to official guidance for checks that require confirmation. It does not provide live flight, queue or gate status, guarantee entry, or make bookings or payments.
defaultPrompt: I have 8 hours at Heathrow. What can I realistically do?
Can I leave Changi Airport during a 7-hour layover?
Compare these two connections and tell me which gives me the better layover.

prompts: I have 8 hours at Heathrow. What can I realistically do?
I have a long connection at Changi. Find food and a shower without making up live availability.
Compare two supplied layovers and tell me which gives more usable time.

positive.description: Core leave-airport decision with conservative deductions and airport caution.
positive.prompt: I have eight hours at Heathrow, from 08:00 to 16:00. Can I visit London?
positive.expected_behavior: Calculate the supplied eight-hour connection conservatively, surface Heathrow's stay-airside guidance, show the airport reserve and explain that entry permission plus current return travel times must be confirmed before an outside plan can be recommended.

positive.description: Duration-only broad planning without invented flight clocks.
positive.prompt: I have eight hours at Heathrow. What should I do?
positive.expected_behavior: Use connectionDurationMinutes=480 with unknown clock strings, give a relative usable-time and return allowance, preserve Heathrow's stay-airside guidance, and do not invent arrival or departure times.

positive.description: Retrieve source-backed airport facilities and official planning links.
positive.prompt: I have a long connection at Singapore Changi. Where can I find food, showers and the terminal map?
positive.expected_behavior: Return attributed static airport essentials and official links, distinguish verified or stale static records from live availability, and avoid claiming current opening status unless the returned evidence supports it.

positive.description: Compare supplied connections by conservative usable time.
positive.prompt: Compare a Singapore connection from 08:00 to 14:00 with one from 08:00 to 16:00. Which gives more usable airport time?
positive.expected_behavior: Assess both connections independently, identify the option with more conservative usable airport time, and state that prices, ticket protection and live delay risk are not compared.

positive.description: Check a named stopover programme without overstating eligibility.
positive.prompt: Does Turkish Airlines offer Touristanbul on an eight-hour connection at Istanbul Airport?
positive.expected_behavior: Return the recorded Touristanbul duration window and official source when available while leaving ticket eligibility, immigration permission, operating dates and seat availability unconfirmed until checked with the operator.

negative.description: Booking and payment are outside Layover Pilot's read-only capability.
negative.prompt: Book my Istanbul tour and pay for lunch.

negative.description: Layover Pilot must not fabricate live flight, gate, queue or public-transport data.
negative.prompt: Tell me the live gate and current delay for BA123 and the immigration queue at Heathrow right now.

negative.description: Layover Pilot is not a flight-search or ticket-purchase service.
negative.prompt: Find and buy the cheapest flight from London to Singapore next Friday.
